claim.claim-text: 1. An industrial system (20) for heating, drying, or curing, comprising:
2. The system (20) of claim 1, further comprising a low-pressure hydrogen storage system (360, 380, 400) for storing the hydrogen fuel produced by the electrolyser (700).
3. The system (20) of any of claims 1-2, further comprising a renewable energy system for powering the electrolyser (700) to produce the hydrogen fuel.

4. The system (20) of any of claims 1-3, further comprising: a liquid propane fuel system for providing a liquid propane fuel to the system (20); and wherein the cooking system includes a fuel control module in operative connection with the processor to control the use of the at least one of the liquid propane fuel or the hydrogen fuel for use by the at least one heating element.

5. The system (20) of any of claims 1-4, further comprising at least one interface configured to facilitate a system external to at least one of: monitoring the system (20), controling the system (20), or obtaining data collected by the system (20) via interaction with the server.
6. The system (20) of any of claims 1-5, further comprising at least one sensor including at least one of a temperature sensor, a weight sensor, a pressure sensor, or a gyro-based sensor.

7. The system (20) of any of claims 1-6, wherein the processor is configured to control the electrolyser (700) by signaling to the electrolyser (700) a demand for the hydrogen fuel such that the electrolyser (700) directs at least one of storing the hydrogen fuel, producing the hydrogen fuel, or indicating the hydrogen fuel as not currently available.
8. The system (20) of any of claims 1-7, wherein the system is configured to produce materials and components through at least one of heating, drying, curing, or treating in a manufacturing process.

9. The system (20) of any of claims 1-8, wherein the at least one heating element is at least one of a burner (30), a gas burner, an electric burner, an induction burner, a convection element, a grilling element, or a radiative element.

10. The system (20) of any of claims 1-9, wherein the electrolyser (700) is configured to produce the hydrogen fuel rather than sourcing the hydrogen fuel from storage based on a contemporaneous demand for the hydrogen fuel and the ability to produce the hydrogen fuel is combined to determine an operation of energy production and consumption.

11. The system (20) of any of claims 1-10, further comprising a fuel mixing device that is controlled automatically based on, at least in part, at least one of historical consumption, historical availability, current consumption, current availability, planned consumption, planned availability, anticipated consumption, or anticipated availability.
12. The system (20) of any of claims 1-11, further comprising a device for converting the hydrogen fuel to produce electricity.
13. The system (20) of any of claims 1-12, further comprising a low-pressure storage for storing the hydrogen fuel as a source of energy that is converted into electricity.

14. The system (20) of any of claims 1-13, wherein the processor is disposed in a housing of a knob such that a user's interaction with the knob is converted to a control message to control the at least one heating element.
